title: Sonnet XVII
author: Pablo Neruda
who: Pablo Neruda (1904 to 1973) was a Chilean poet and diplomat who received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1971. He wrote in Spanish, so in English the wording depends on the translator.
why: The poem comes from Cien sonetos de amor (One Hundred Love Sonnets), published in 1959 and dedicated to Matilde Urrutia, who became his wife. I do not know of a documented account of this single sonnet's writing beyond that.
notice: Notice that the poem begins by saying how the speaker does not love, before it says how he does. Watch which things are compared to love and which are refused. Notice how plain the closing lines are after the images that come before.
prompts: Describe someone you love without using any of the usual comparisons. What is left?
What do you love in a person that nobody else would think to praise?
